PullRequest.Title: agentHost: only restrict GitHub MCP servers in Agent Merge turns
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Agent Merge turns blocked MCP in general, not just GitHub. #333872 enforced "use only the Agent Merge GitHub tools" by treating every external MCP server as a GitHub fallback:

- **Copilot** denied tools from every registered server (root config, workspace `.mcp.json`, and plugins).
- **Claude** denied every `mcp__*` tool except the host server tools, including the workbench client tools (`mcp__client__*`).
- **Codex** dropped all configured MCP servers from the thread.

Unrelated local servers such as Component Explorer were therefore rejected with a GitHub-specific denial, and the agent stopped the turn.

## Changes

- Add `isAgentMergeRestrictedMcpServer`, which identifies a GitHub MCP server by its name, a GitHub-hosted endpoint (`github.com`, `githubcopilot.com`, `ghe.com`), or a command that runs `github-mcp-server` or `@modelcontextprotocol/server-github`.
- Copilot and Claude now deny tools only from those servers and the built-in `github-mcp-server`. Codex omits only those servers during Agent Merge turns.
- The GitHub CLI, direct GitHub API, and GitHub tool-name restrictions are unchanged.

## Notes for reviewers

- The Copilot and Claude pre-tool hooks receive only a tool name. Servers the SDK loads without the host seeing their configuration (for example Claude user-level config) are therefore matched by name only.
- Non-GitHub MCP servers are usable again during Agent Merge turns, including a custom server that could itself reach GitHub. The Agent Merge prompt still requires the dedicated tools for CI details, review threads, and workflow reruns.

## Validation

- Added tests for the shared classifier and for each provider. The provider tests fail against the previous implementation.
- The related agent host unit suites pass (1370 tests), and eslint and hygiene are clean on the changed files.

Scenarios.Scenario: Codex Agent Merge session start, resume, and launch reconciliation with configured MCP servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session MCP discovery and configuration assembly precede the existing thread/start or resume IPC. The diff adds an in-memory filter and includes enabled non-GitHub server configs in that existing request; downstream server readiness is managed by Codex and is not shown as a host-side serial wait.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh workspace MCP discovery before session start or resume.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per materialization/resume, covering the workspace definitions as a group.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery refresh ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the session's MCP configuration is sent to Codex.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the effective MCP server configuration in the existing Codex thread/start or resume request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One host IPC request per thread start/resume; the payload contains one entry per effective enabled non-GitHub server during Agent Merge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The IPC already occurred, but Agent Merge supplied no configured MCP server entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration delivery is on thread initialization; individual MCP readiness is delegated to Codex.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/codex/codexAgent.ts:_buildSessionMcpServers at changed lines 2792-2794, consumed by thread configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Codex may launch/connect each configured non-GitHub MCP server for the thread.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one launch/connection per effective configured non-GitHub server per thread start or restart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Merge omitted every configured MCP server, so none of these intended non-GitHub servers were available or launched for that turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed to expose those servers' tools; exact readiness scheduling is owned by Codex and not established as a serial host critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of enabled root, workspace, and client-plugin MCP servers after name collision merging; each configured name appears once in the effective record.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The host sends one thread/start/resume request containing the merged server record. There is no changed host-side per-server async loop; Codex app-server owns any downstream launch concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Root and workspace definitions are rebuilt as before; auth tokens are reused from the existing token map. The diff adds no cache or retry behavior, and warm signature checks repeat only the bounded in-memory filtering.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the single merged configuration request and one effective entry per server; no evidence that the diff creates repeated per-item host boundary calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not expose Codex's downstream per-server launch concurrency or readiness latency, but typical configured-server cardinality is bounded by user/workspace configuration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Restoring configured non-GitHub MCP servers necessarily restores their normal per-thread launch/connect work; the diff groups them in the existing thread request and does not add accidental retries, serialization, or duplicate launches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Claude session materialization/rebuild and Agent Merge pre-tool authorization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing endpoint resolution, MCP discovery/plugin parsing, and SDK startup remain on materialization/rebuild. The diff adds linear in-memory classification over already loaded definitions and a synchronous set/name check before each tool use.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the built-in GitHub MCP endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per materialization or rebuild when authenticated and enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same endpoint resolution occurred before the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh MCP discovery and parse applicable client plugin definitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery refresh plus one parse for each applicable synced plugin per materialization/rebuild.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refresh and plugin parsing occurred; the diff only classifies their already parsed definitions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start or rebuild the Claude SDK process with MCP wiring.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK startup per materialization or rebuild.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SDK startup already received the same MCP server wiring.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the session pipeline is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke an allowed non-GitHub remote MCP tool selected by the agent during Agent Merge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One boundary call per agent-selected MCP tool invocation, not per configured server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All external MCP tool calls were denied during Agent Merge, including unrelated servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the selected tool call blocks its dependent turn progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured/discovered MCP definitions at materialization, plus one check per attempted tool call. The restricted-name set deduplicates by server name.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Startup steps remain awaited in the existing sequence. The pre-tool hook is synchronous and performs no boundary call; actual MCP invocation concurrency remains SDK-controlled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A restricted-name Set is built once per materialization/rebuild and reused by all pre-tool checks for that pipeline. Existing discovery refresh and plugin parsing behavior is unchanged; there is no new negative-cache retry state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff adds no startup boundary and reuses one Set for hook checks; enabled tool calls are one-for-one with requested behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact server count and tool-call latency depend on user configuration, but classification itself is bounded and boundary calls occur only when selected by the agent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added CPU/allocation is small linear startup work plus constant-time hook lookup, while newly allowed non-GitHub calls are the intended functionality and are not fanned out automatically.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot session snapshot setup and Agent Merge pre-tool authorization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session construction scans the already supplied snapshot once to build the restricted-name Set. Each pre-tool hook reuses that Set; no changed I/O precedes authorization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke an allowed non-GitHub remote MCP tool selected during Agent Merge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per selected tool invocation; no automatic invocation per configured server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every snapshot MCP server name was treated as restricted, so these unrelated tool calls were denied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only a selected tool's request is on its dependent turn path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke an allowed local MCP server tool selected during Agent Merge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per selected local MCP tool invocation; process ownership/startup is existing runtime behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-tool hook denied tools from every configured local MCP server during Agent Merge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only selected tool execution affects turn progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Root and plugin MCP servers in the client snapshot at construction, then one prefix check across only restricted server names per attempted tool call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Construction is synchronous. Tool-hook calls may be issued by the runtime, but each performs only local checks; downstream MCP concurrency is unchanged and runtime-controlled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The filtered restricted server names are cached in a Set for the session lifetime. No discovery, endpoint, or tool-result cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that construction is one bounded snapshot scan and hooks reuse the Set; the diff reduces the checked-name set relative to the previous all-server Set.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Snapshot size and MCP call duration vary by installation, but no changed code automatically executes all allowed tools.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The one-time classifier scan is bounded, per-hook work is not materially amplified, and newly reachable MCP boundaries occur only for explicitly selected tools as required.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all eight changed files and all three provider paths. Checked startup/rebuild work, per-tool hooks, configured-server cardinality, signature reconciliation, discovery/filesystem work, IPC, subprocess/network reachability, caching, and concurrency. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
